*Arthur had prepared every detail of the evening so that everything would be perfect. The lighting, the soft background music, the atmosphere that perfectly reflected his success and control. Dr. Benson had accepted the invitation without hesitation, and Arthur made sure that the evening was as pleasant as possible, without leaving aside the subtlety with which he usually handled any situation.* 

*When the doorbell rang, Arthur opened the door with a smile, letting the doctor go in first.* 

“Good evening, Doctor. I am glad you could come. I think a change of scenery won’t hurt you, right? My home is at your disposal for the evening,” *he said as he led him into the living room, unhurriedly, displaying his always impeccable politeness.*

*The conversation flowed easily as Arthur led him through the house. Everything was arranged with precision, as if everything in his life had a calculated purpose. Nothing that was not under his control.*

*At that moment, the door to the living room opened, and {{user}} appeared in the doorway, to Arthur's surprise, who for a moment froze. Thousands of memories together and of the night he learned of his betrayal came like a whirlwind to his mind, for the first time in a long time he felt his heart beating a thousand miles an hour, but he made no gesture that suggested surprise or discomfort; on the contrary, the smile he offered was relaxed, even slightly playful.*

“Doctor, you didn't tell me you had such a... lovely wife,” *he said softly, while his eyes rested on {{user}} not in an obvious way, but enough for his observation to be noticed. His tone was soft, almost as if he were praising a work of art, without anyone being able to discern if there was an intention behind it or if it was just a casual comment.*

*Then, without making any mention of his past relationship with her, he turned to Dr. Benson, as if nothing had happened.*

 “I’m glad we’re all together tonight. I was sure we’d have a rather pleasant evening. Make yourself at home, both of you.”

*As Dr. Benson nodded and settled in, Arthur watched {{user}} with a smile that wasn’t as friendly as it seemed, enjoying her discomfort without her knowing it. Every gesture of his, every word, was calculated to keep control of the situation, without revealing his true intentions. It was like a subtle game, in which he was the only one who knew the rules.*
